Consider the following PR description:
Error message formatting inconsistency with quoted tag options

#### Description

When an unsupported tag option is encountered, the error message formatting is inconsistent. The tag option value is not properly quoted in the error message, which can lead to confusion when debugging issues with tag options that contain special characters or spaces.

#### Steps/Code to Reproduce

```go
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"github.com/caarlos0/env/v11"
)

type Config struct {
	Value string `env:"VALUE,not_supported!"`
}

func main() {
	var cfg Config
	err := env.Parse(&cfg)
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Printf("Error: %s\n", err.Error())
		// Expected: env: tag option "not_supported!" not supported
		// Actual: env: tag option not_supported! not supported
	}
}
```

The error message should include quotes around the tag option name for clarity, especially when the tag option contains special characters like exclamation marks or other punctuation that might make the error message ambiguous.
</pr_description>

// An aggregated error wrapper to combine gathered errors.
// This allows either to display all errors or convert them individually
// List of the available errors
// ParseError

// NoSupportedTagOptionError
// VarIsNotSetError
// EmptyVarError
// LoadFileContentError
// ParseValueError
type AggregateError struct {
	Errors []error
}

func newAggregateError(initErr error) error {
	return AggregateError{
		[]error{
			initErr,
		},
	}
}

func (e AggregateError) Error() string {
	var sb strings.Builder

	sb.WriteString("env:")

	for _, err := range e.Errors {
		sb.WriteString(fmt.Sprintf(" %v;", err.Error()))
	}

	return strings.TrimRight(sb.String(), ";")
}

// Unwrap implements std errors.Join go1.20 compatibility
func (e AggregateError) Unwrap() []error {
	return e.Errors
}

// Is conforms with errors.Is.
func (e AggregateError) Is(err error) bool {
	for _, ie := range e.Errors {
		if reflect.TypeOf(ie) == reflect.TypeOf(err) {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}
